optimizedCv.targetRoleTitle: Service Analytics Analyst, Lift and Escalator Maintenance
professionalSummary: Service Data Analyst with experience designing SQL data models for lift callout logs, analysing repeat faults, publishing monthly performance reports, and building Power BI dashboards for branch managers and key accounts.
experienceHighlights: Designed the callout fact table and equipment/site dimensions in SQL Server, loading handheld callout logs nightly (src_2280af42b2bf).
Analysed repeat callouts on hydraulic lifts, introduced a door‑operator inspection step, reducing repeat callouts from 11.8% to 7.1% over a 12‑month period (src_1a91696064e7).
Published monthly contract performance reports covering response times, first‑time fix rate, and open faults for eleven key accounts and four branch managers (src_c38fb1b11d07).
Listed lifts by fault frequency each quarter to aid planners in scheduling preventive visits (src_2bd71fda304f).
Built and refreshed branch dashboards in Power BI after each nightly load (src_a744d78dcd9d).
projectsAndWorkSamples: Repeat‑callout review pack for the south branch, including callout‑system extracts for July‑December 2022 (11.8%) and July‑December 2023 (7.1%), definition of repeat callout, and branch manager sign‑off dated 15 January 2024 (src_0a0a905052d1).
optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The provided resume and work sample establish the candidate’s experience with SQL data modelling, repeat fault analysis, monthly reporting, preventive maintenance support, and Power BI dashboard creation. They do not provide evidence of production‑level deployment, ownership of the entire data model lifecycle, or row‑level security implementation details.

decisionBoundary.statement: Human review is required to assess fit based on evidence gaps and interview signals.

role.roleTitle: Service Analytics Analyst, Lift and Escalator Maintenance

evidence.text: Designed the callout fact table and the equipment and site dimensions in SQL Server at Ardent Lift Services, loading the handheld callout logs every night.
evidence.notes: Direct statement of SQL data model design and nightly load.

evidence.text: Analysed repeat callouts on hydraulic lifts and, with the technical support engineers, introduced a door-operator inspection step. Repeat callouts within 30 days on the south branch went from 11.8% of callouts in July to December 2022 to 7.1% in July to December 2023.
evidence.notes: Shows repeat fault analysis and measured reduction.

evidence.text: Published the monthly contract performance report (response times, first-time fix rate, open faults) for eleven key accounts and the four branch managers.
Each quarter, listed lifts by fault frequency so that the planners could book preventive visits for the most fault-prone units first.
evidence.notes: Shows support for preventive maintenance planning.

evidence.text: Built the branch dashboards in Power BI and refreshed them after each nightly load.
evidence.notes: Confirms dashboard creation but lacks explicit mention of row‑level security.

missingEvidence: Evidence that dashboards include row‑level security by branch
